'''Johnathan Lee Williams  III''' (born May 22, 1995) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Phoenix Super LPG Fuel Masters]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] (PBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]].<ref name="GU Profile">{{cite web|title=Gonzaga Basketball Profile: Johnathan Williams|url=http://www.gozags.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/johnathan_williams_982243.html|access-date=April 4, 2016}}</ref> He spent two seasons with the [[University of Missouri]] [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Tigers men's basketball team]] before deciding to transfer before the 2015–16 season.

==High school career==
Williams attended Southwind High School in Memphis, Tennessee for four years, finishing his high school tenure with an 88–17 record and earning a starting spot on the basketball team from the get-go in his freshman year. As a freshman, he averaged 10.2 points and 9.5 rebounds, leading his squad to a 26–5 record and second-place at state, and was named an honorable mention freshman All-American by [[CBS Interactive#MaxPreps|Max Preps]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Boys Basketball Freshmen All-American Team|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/hy74Hj0cEd-lugAcxJTdpg/boys-basketball-freshmen-all-american-team.htm|date=April 27, 2010}}</ref> During his sophomore year, Williams averaged 17.3 points, 11.5 rebounds, 2.1 assists, and 3 blocks, while 52 percent from the field, 48 percent from 3-point, and 80 percent from the free-throw line, as well as a 26–6 record and third-place at the state tournament. As a junior, he averaged 15.7 points, 10.2 rebounds, 2.6 assists, 2.6 blocks, and 1.1 assists, while guiding his team to a 28–5 record and an appearance in the state quarterfinals.<ref name="USA Basketball">{{cite web|title=USA Basketball Profile: Johnathan Williams|url=http://archive.usab.com/bios/williams_johnathan.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160418121521/http://archive.usab.com/bios/williams_johnathan.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 18, 2016|date=July 10, 2012}}</ref> Williams capped off his incredible high school career by averaging 18.9 points and 9.5 rebounds, while leading Southwind to a 34–6 record and a state title. He earned  all-state honors by the Tennessee Sports Writers Association in 2011, 2012, and 2013.<ref name="Mizzou">{{cite web|title=Missouri Basketball Profile: Johnathan Williams|url=http://www.mutigers.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=3402|access-date=April 4, 2016}}</ref>

===Recruiting===
{{quote box|width=23em|align=right|quote="Johnathan is so versatile on the floor and has a number of ways he can impact a basketball game. His size and skillset are unique and he can present mismatch problems for opponents. He is smooth on the perimeter and is long and active and really has a great feel for how to attack his opponent and keep his teammates involved. Off the court Johnathan is just such a complete young man. He comes from a tremendous family and has a great sense of what it takes to be a leader on the court, in the classroom and amongst his teammates."|source=— [[Frank Haith]], Missouri Head Coach.<ref name="signing">{{cite web|title=MIZZOU BASKETBALL ANNOUNCES NATIONALLY RANKED SIGNING CLASS|url=http://www.mutigers.com/news/2012/11/14/Mizzou_Basketball_Announces_Nationally_Ranked_Signing_Class.aspx?path=mbball|date=November 14, 2012}}</ref>}}
After taking official visits to Georgetown, Missouri, Tennessee, Michigan State, and George Mason, Johnathan Williams commit to Missouri.<ref>{{cite web|title=Memphis forward picks Mizzou|url=https://basketballrecruiting.n.rivals.com/news/memphis-forward-picks-mizzou|date=October 18, 2012}}</ref> Williams signed with Missouri during the early signing period in November 2012.<ref name="signing"/>

==College career==

===Freshman season===
As a freshman at Missouri, Johnathan Williams helped to lead to Tigers to an appearance in the NIT and a 23–13 record, and started every game, while averaging 5.8 points, along with team highs of 6.5 rebounds and 1.6 blocks per game. His 227 total rebounds were 11th best in the SEC in 2013–14 and the 4th-most as a freshman at Missouri. His 57 total blocks were 5th-best in the SEC, along with the 8th-best nationally among freshmen, 2nd most by a freshman at Missouri and 5th-most as a Tiger regardless of class.<ref name="Mizzou"/>

In his first collegiate game in an 89–53 win over [[Southeastern Louisiana Lions basketball|Southeastern Louisiana]] on November 8, 2013, Williams posted 7 points, 6 rebounds, and 1 assist on 2-for-2 field goals and 3-of-4 free throws.<ref>{{cite web|title=MIZZOU TAKES 2013–14 SEASON OPENER, 89–53|url=http://www.mutigers.com/news/2013/11/8/Mizzou_Takes_2013_14_Season_Opener_89_53.aspx?path=mbball|date=November 8, 2013}}</ref> On November 23, Williams grabbed career-highs of 17 rebounds and 2 steals to go along with 7 points, 3 blocks, and 2 assists on 3-for-10 field goals and 1-of-4 free throws in a win over [[Gardner–Webb Runnin' Bulldogs men's basketball|Gardner-Webb]].<ref>{{cite web|title=MISSOURI DOWNS GARDNER-WEBB, 72–63|url=http://www.mutigers.com/news/2013/11/23/Missouri_Downs_Gardner_Webb_72_63.aspx?path=mbball|date=November 23, 2013}}</ref> He had a season-high 14 points, along with 8 rebounds, 1 assist, and 1 steal on 3-for-3 from the field and 8-for-10 from the charity stripe in a win against [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern]] on November 28.<ref>{{cite web|title=MISSOURI OVERCOMES NORTHWESTERN, 78–67|url=http://www.mutigers.com/news/2013/11/29/Missouri_Overcomes_Northwestern_78_67.aspx?path=mbball|date=November 28, 2013}}</ref> On December 7 in an 80–71 win over #18 [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], he had 10 points, 15 rebounds, 2 blocks, 1 steal, and 1 assist on 3-of-5 field goals and 4-of-6 free throws.<ref>{{cite web|title=MIZZOU TOPS NO. 18 UCLA, 80–71|url=http://www.mutigers.com/news/2013/12/7/Mizzou_Tops_No_18_UCLA_80_71.aspx?path=mbball|date=December 7, 2013}}</ref> On March 5, 2014, Williams blocked a career-high 5 shots, along with 7 points and 8 rebounds on 3-of-7 field goals and 1-of-2 free throws, in a win over [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]].<ref>{{cite web|title=ROSS SAVES SENIOR NIGHT FOR MIZZOU, 57–56|url=http://www.mutigers.com/news/2014/3/5/Ross_Saves_Senior_Night_For_Mizzou_57_56.aspx?path=mbball|date=March 5, 2014}}</ref> In a double-overtime win over Texas A&M in the SEC Tournament on March 13, Williams dished out a career-high 4 assists to go along with a double-double (11 points and 15 rebounds), 2 blocks, and 1 steal on 3-of-7 2-pointers, 1-for-2 from 3-point land, and 2-of-2 free throw shooting.<ref>{{cite web|title=TIGERS OUTLAST A&M IN TWO OT'S, 91–83|url=http://www.mutigers.com/news/2014/3/13/Tigers_Outlast_A_amp_M_in_Two_OT_s_91_83.aspx?path=mbball|date=March 13, 2014}}</ref>

===Sophomore season===
Heading into his sophomore year, Williams was expected to shoulder a much larger role for Missouri with the losses of guards [[Jabari Brown]], [[Jordan Clarkson]], and [[Earnest Ross]], who combined to average more than 50 points per game, as well as head coach [[Frank Haith]]. Williams was Missouri's top returning scorer, rebounder, and shot-blocker. However, tough times were ahead for Williams as he suffered a partial meniscus tear in his right knee during the preseason of early October 2014.<ref name="recovery">{{cite web|title=Missouri forward Johnathan Williams still battling knee injury|url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/sec/university-of-missouri/article3425301.html|date=October 28, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Missouri forward Johnathan Williams III out with torn meniscus|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/24733202/missouri-forward-johnathan-williams-iii-out-with-torn-meniscus|date=October 1, 2014}}</ref>

Despite leading Missouri in scoring (11.9 points), rebounding (7.1 rebounds), and shot-blocking (0.6) per game during his sophomore season, Williams was hampered all season by a torn meniscus, and the Tigers finished with the most losses and longest losing streak (13) in school history with a 9–23 record.<ref>{{cite web|title=Missouri's Johnathan Williams III will transfer|url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/sec/university-of-missouri/article17015117.html|date=March 31, 2015}}</ref><ref name="transfer">{{cite web|title=Mizzou's Williams decides to transfer|url=http://www.stltoday.com/sports/college/mizzou/mizzou-s-williams-decides-to-transfer/article_9bbd0fa8-bead-5ebb-bef0-7d829de37baa.html|date=March 31, 2015}}</ref>

In the regular season opener in a 69–61 loss to [[Kansas City Roos men's basketball|UMKC]] on November 14, 2014, Williams had a season high of 4 blocks, along with 6 points and 5 rebounds on 3-of-7 field goals.<ref>{{cite web|title=MIZZOU DROPS REGULAR SEASON OPENER, 69–61, TO UMKC|url=http://www.mutigers.com/news/2014/11/14/mizzou_drops_regular_season_opener_69_61_to_umkc.aspx|date=November 14, 2014}}</ref> On December 2, he dropped 18 points, 11 rebounds, 1 assist, and 1 block on 5-for-9 field goals and 8-for-14 free throws in a win over [[Southeast Missouri State Redhawks men's basketball|Southeast Missouri State]].<ref>{{cite web|title=TIGERS USE LATE SURGE TO CLIP REDHAWKS, 65–61|url=http://www.mutigers.com/news/2014/12/2/Tigers_Use_Late_Surge_to_Clip_Redhawks_65_61.aspx?path=mbball|date=December 2, 2014}}</ref> In an overtime loss to [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]] on December 30, Williams scored 22 points, along with 9 rebounds, 1 assist, and 1 steal on 6-of-10 2-point field goals, 2-of-3 3-pointers, and 4-of-7 free throws.<ref>{{cite web|title=MIZZOU FALLS IN OVERTIME TO OKLAHOMA STATE, 74–72|url=http://www.mutigers.com/news/2014/12/30/Mizzou_Falls_in_Overtime_to_Oklahoma_State_74_72.aspx?path=mbball|date=December 30, 2014}}</ref> On January 8, 2015, he had double-double (21 points and 10 rebounds) and 1 block on 8-for-17 field goal shooting and 5-for-8 free throws in a 74–67 win in overtime over LSU in the SEC opener.<ref>{{cite web|title=MIZZOU HOLDS OFF LSU, 74–67, IN OVERTIME SEC OPENER|url=http://www.mutigers.com/news/2015/1/8/Mizzou_Holds_Off_LSU_74_67_in_Overtime_SEC_Opener.aspx?path=mbball|date=January 8, 2015}}</ref> Williams had career-highs of 27 points and 3-of-5 from beyond the 3-point arc, along with 7 rebounds, 2 assists, and 1 block, on 6-for-10 2-pointers and 6-for-8 from the free throw line in a 77–74 loss against [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State]] on February 14. He scored 23 of his points in the second half, including a 3-pointer which brought Mizzou within 1 with 2 seconds remaining, but it wasn't enough.<ref>{{cite web|title=MIZZOU HOLDS OFF LSU, 74–67, IN OVERTIME SEC OPENER|url=http://www.mutigers.com/news/2015/2/14/Tigers_Nearly_There_Against_Mississippi_State_But_Drop_77_74_Result.aspx?path=mbball|date=January 8, 2015}}</ref>

===Junior season===
{{quote box|width=23em|align=right|quote="Johnathan is a very high character young man, and really good academically,” head coach Mark Few said. “He’s a proven commodity at high Division I level in scoring and rebounding, and he fits a real need for where our team and personnel makeup will be a year from now. I think this next year of development will be huge for him. It’s a perfect scenario with being able to work with [[Nigel Williams-Goss|Nigel [Williams-Goss]]] and also, day-in and day-out, go against [[Kyle Wiltjer|Kyle [Wiltjer]]], [[Domantas Sabonis|Domantas [Sabonis]]] and [[Przemek Karnowski|Przemek [Karnowski]]]. That really creates a great situation for him development-wise."|source=— [[Mark Few]], Gonzaga Head Coach.<ref name="GU transfer">{{cite web|title=Gonzaga MBB Adds Missouri Transfer Johnathan Williams|url=http://www.gozags.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/060415aab.html|date=June 4, 2015}}</ref>}}

After his 2014–15 campaign with Missouri, Williams decided to transfer. His father cited that Williams didn't fit in with his teammates and didn't believe he was developing enough. His father thought the a redshirt year to "get stronger, work on ball skills and get that knee a chance to heal."<ref name="transfer"/> Missouri restricted Williams from transferring to 25 schools, including every SEC and Big-12 school, along with Arizona and Illinois.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Missouri transfer Johnathan Williams III restricted from 25 schools|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball-news/4641048-missouri-hoops-transfer-restricted-from-going-to-25-schools-jonathan-williams-iii|date=April 8, 2015}}</ref> Williams took official visits to Gonzaga, Georgetown, and SMU, but made the decision to transfer to Gonzaga. Williams would have to redshirt the 2015–16 season before having two years of eligibility to play at the beginning of the 2016–17 season.<ref name="GU transfer"/><ref>{{cite web|title=Missouri transfer Williams picks Gonzaga|url=http://www.spokesman.com/blogs/sportslink/2015/may/30/missouri-transfer-williams-picks-gonzaga/|date=May 30, 2015}}</ref>

===Senior season===
As a senior at Gonzaga, Williams led the team in scoring (13.4 points per game) and rebounding (8.5 per game). He was an All-[[West Coast Conference]] selection and was AP All-America honorable mention.<ref name=israel>{{cite news |last1=Meehan |first1=Jim |title=Former Gonzaga standout Johnathan Williams signs with pro team in Israel |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2019/aug/05/former-gonzaga-standout-johnathan-williams-signs-w/ |access-date=June 23, 2020 |work=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |date=August 5, 2019}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Los Angeles Lakers (2018–2019)===
After going undrafted in the [[2018 NBA draft]], Williams signed a contract offer from the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] to be on their [[NBA Summer League|Summer League]] team roster.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Meehan |first1=Jim |title=Former Gonzaga forward Johnathan Williams signs NBA Summer League contract with Los Angeles Lakers |url=http://www.spokesman.com/stories/2018/jun/22/former-gonzaga-forward-johnathan-williams-signs-nb/ |access-date=June 24, 2018 |work=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |date=June 22, 2018}}</ref> On July 21, 2018, Williams signed with the Lakers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/180721sign-johnathan-williams|title=Lakers Sign Johnathan Williams|work=NBA.com|date=July 21, 2018|access-date=July 21, 2018}}</ref> He was waived on October 13, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/lakers-waive-machado-and-williams|title=Lakers Waive Machado and Williams|work=NBA.com|date=October 13, 2018|access-date=October 16, 2018}}</ref> Williams then signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Lakers on October 19, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign Johnathan Williams to Two-Way Contract; Waive Travis Wear|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/181019-lakers-sign-johnathan-williams-two-way-contract-waive-travis-wear|work=NBA.com|access-date=October 19, 2018|date=October 19, 2018}}</ref> On March 9, 2019, Williams scored his career-high 18 points with ten rebounds, an assist and a block in a 120–107 loss to the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071662|title=Kyrie's 30 propel Celtics past LeBron's Lakers, 120–107|work=ESPN.com|date=March 9, 2019|access-date=March 9, 2019}}</ref> Williams averaged 6.5 points and 4.1 rebounds per game for the Lakers and 15.2 points and 8.7 rebounds per game in the G League.<ref name=israel/>

On June 30, 2019, Williams joined the [[Houston Rockets]] for the 2019 [[NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/rockets/article/How-the-Rockets-roster-shapes-up-for-Summer-League-14074481.php|title=How the Rockets roster shapes up for Summer League|work=Houston Chronicle|date=July 5, 2019|first=Jonathan|last=Feigen}}</ref> He averaged 8.4 points and 6.0 rebounds per game in five games.<ref name=israel/>

===Maccabi Rishon LeZion (2019)===
On July 30, 2019, Williams signed with [[Maccabi Rishon LeZion (basketball)|Maccabi Rishon LeZion]] of the [[Israel Basketball Premier League|Israel Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Askounis|first1=John|title=Maccabi Rishon LeZion lands Johnathan Williams|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/eurocup/913504/maccabi-rishon-lezion-lands-johnathan-williams/|website=Eurohoops|access-date=July 30, 2019|date=July 30, 2019}}</ref> On November 13, 2019, Williams recorded a double-double of 11 rebounds and a career-high 19 points, while shooting 7-of-11 from the field, in a 79–85 loss to [[Virtus Pallacanestro Bologna|Virtus Bologna]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Maccabi Rishon LeZion vs. Segafredo Virtus Bologna – Game|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/eurocup/game-center/?seasoncode=U2019&gamecode=75|website=EuroCupBasketball|access-date=December 23, 2019|date=November 13, 2019}}</ref> In 18 games played for Rishon LeZion, he averaged 11.7 points and 9.1 rebounds per game. On December 23, 2019, he parted ways with Rishon LeZion after receiving offers from NBA teams.<ref>{{cite web|title=ג'ונתן וויליאמס שוחרר מראשל"צ, בדרך ל-NBA|url=https://www.one.co.il/Article/350137.html|website=ONE.co.il|access-date=December 23, 2019|date=December 23, 2019|language=he}}</ref>

===Washington Wizards (2019–2020)===
[[File:Johnathan Williams.jpg|thumb|right|Williams with the [[Washington Wizards]] in 2020]]
On December 26, 2019, Williams signed with the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-sign-johnathan-williams|title=Wizards sign Johnathan Williams|work=NBA.com|date=December 26, 2019|access-date=December 26, 2019}}</ref> On January 4, 2020, Williams was waived by the Wizards after appearing in 6 games for the team.<ref>{{cite web|title=Wizards waive Johnathan Williams|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-waive-johnathan-williams|date=January 4, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 4, 2019}}</ref> Eight days later on January 12, 2020, the [[Washington Wizards]] announced that they had signed Williams to a [[two-way contract]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Wizards sign Johnathan Williams to two-way contract|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-sign-johnathan-williams-two-way-contract|date=January 12, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 12, 2020}}</ref> In the G League, Williams averaged 13.1 points, 9.6 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 1.1 blocks per game.<ref name="Yahyabeyoglu" />

===Galatasaray (2020–2021)===
On September 6, 2020, Williams signed with [[Galatasaray S.K. (men's basketball)|Galatasaray]] of the Turkish [[Basketball Super League]] (BSL).<ref name="Yahyabeyoglu">{{cite web |last1=Yahyabeyoglu |first1=Fersu |title=Galatasaray lands Johnathan Williams III |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Turkey/news/643549/Galatasaray-lands-Johnathan-Williams-III |website=Eurobasket |access-date=September 6, 2020 |date=September 6, 2020}}</ref>

===Niners Chemnitz (2021)===
On February 24, 2021, he signed with [[Niners Chemnitz]] of the German [[Basketball Bundesliga]] (BBL).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/johnathan-williams-signs-with-chemnitz/|title=Johnathan Williams signs with Chemnitz|last=|first=|date=February 24, 2021|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=February 24, 2021}}</ref>

===Aquila Basket Trento (2021–2022)===
On August 21, 2021, Williams signed with [[Aquila Basket Trento|Dolomiti Energia Trento]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Johnathan Williams officially signs with Trento |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/johnathan-williams-officially-signs-with-trento/ |website=Sportando |access-date=August 21, 2021 |date=August 21, 2021}}</ref>

===Fighting Eagles Nagoya (2022–2023)===
On July 1, 2022, Williams signed with [[Fighting Eagles Nagoya]] of the [[B.League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=【#14 ジョナサン・ウィリアムズ選手】新規入団のお知らせ |url=https://www.fightingeagles.jp/news/detail/id=14891 |website=ファイティングイーグルス名古屋 |access-date=November 2, 2024 |date=July 1, 2022}}</ref>

===Phoenix Super LPG Fuel Masters (2023–2024)===
In October 2023, Williams signed with the [[Phoenix Super LPG Fuel Masters]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] (PBA) as the team's import for the [[2023–24 PBA Commissioner's Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://pba.ph/news/new-faces-out-to-steal-thunder-from-brownlee-rhj|title=New faces out to steal thunder from Brownlee, RHJ|website=PBA.ph|date=October 12, 2023|accessdate=October 12, 2023}}</ref>

===Toyama Grouses (2024)===
On March 19, 2024, Williams signed with [[Toyama Grouses]] of the [[B.League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=ジョナサン・ウィリアムズ選手(新規) 契約締結のお知らせ |url=https://grouses.jp/news/detail/id=20924 |website=富山グラウジーズ |access-date=November 2, 2024 |date=March 19, 2024}}</ref>

===Veltex Shizuoka (2024)===
On November 1, 2024, Williams signed a short-term contract with [[Veltex Shizuoka]] of the [[B.League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=#2 ジョナサン・ウィリアムズ選手 契約合意（新規）のお知らせ |url=https://veltex.co.jp/news/detail/id=47558 |website=ベルテックス静岡 |access-date=November 2, 2024 |date=November 1, 2024}}</ref> On December 4, his contract was ended.<ref>{{cite web |title=#2 ジョナサン・ウィリアムズ選手 短期契約終了のお知らせ |url=https://veltex.co.jp/news/detail/id=47651 |website=ベルテックス静岡 |access-date=December 4, 2024 |date=December 4, 2024}}</ref>

===Chiba Jets (2024–2025)===
On December 6, 2024, Williams signed with [[Chiba Jets]] of the [[B.League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=2024-25シーズン 新規契約選手のお知らせ |url=https://chibajets.jp/news/detail/id=23156 |website=千葉ジェッツ |access-date=December 6, 2024 |date=December 6, 2024}}</ref> On January 31, 2025, his contract was terminated.<ref>{{cite web |title=ジョナサン・ウィリアムズ選手 契約解除のお知らせ |url=https://chibajets.jp/news/detail/id=23262 |website=千葉ジェッツ |access-date=February 1, 2025 |date=January 31, 2025}}</ref>

===London Lions (2025–present)===
On August 2, 2025, Williams signed a year long contract with [[London Lions]] of the [[Super League Basketball|SLB]] and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Johnathan Williams III and Peyton Aldridge bounce back in EuroCup|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/eurocup/1853777/johnathan-williams-iii-signs-with-london-lions-eurocup/| website=www.eurohoops.net| date=2025-08-03| access-date=2025-08-03}}</ref>

===Phoenix Super LPG Fuel Masters (2026)===
On April 30, 2026, Williams returns to Phoenix for his 2nd stint with the team.<ref>{{cite web |first=Matthew |last=Li |url=https://tiebreakertimes.com.ph/tbt/johnathan-williams-returns-as-phoenix-gambles-on-proven-import-in-crucial-run/373798 |title=Johnathan Williams returns as Phoenix gambles on proven import in crucial run |website=Tiebreaker Times |date=April 30, 2026 |access-date=April 30, 2026 }}</ref>

==National team career==
Johnathan Williams helped the USA win a gold medal in the 2011 [[FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship|FIBA Americas U16 Championship]], while averaging 5.4 points and 4.6 rebounds. In 2012, Williams joined the US and won a gold medal in the [[2012 FIBA Under-17 World Championship|FIBA U17 World Championship]], while averaging 7 points and 4.6 rebounds in 16 minutes per game.<ref name="USA Basketball"/>
